CT4101 Topic Guide

Data Preparation

Make inputs meaningful and comparable before a model sees them.

Exam-use protocol

Before writing, identify the command word: calculate/trace requires an ordered derivation; explain requires a definition, mechanism and assumption; compare/design requires matched criteria, a justified choice and a limitation. The topic-specific recall and worked routes below are the material to adapt—not text to copy blindly.

Part-by-part recall: definitions, assumptions and mechanics

Definitions: preparation handles missingness, encoding, scaling and leakage. Standardisation z=(x-mu)/sigma is fitted on training data only; distance methods are scale-sensitive. Question cue: name defect, transformation, fitting split and algorithm consequence.

Worked practice 1 — paper-style synthesis (recurring-topic pattern; not a quoted paper prompt) scaling

Question demand: Prepare age (0-100) and income (0-100000) for kNN. Plan/choice: prevent income dominating Euclidean distance. Worked answer: fit min-max or z-score parameters on training data, transform validation/test with them, then use distance. Mark-winning points: no test leakage. Common trap: numeric category codes imply order.

Worked practice 2 — synthesis / design

Question demand: Prepare clinical data with missing values and rare outcome. Plan/choice: profile missing mechanism, impute within pipeline, encode/scale and stratify split. Worked answer: preserve a missingness indicator where informative; fit imputer/scaler on folds; evaluate recall/precision. Mark-winning points: data provenance and leakage control. Common trap: delete rows automatically.

Purpose and relevance

Preprocessing removes avoidable distortions: missing values, incompatible scales, and categories that algorithms cannot directly use. It is especially important for distance-based methods.

What a question really asks — answer plan

“Why normalise?” asks for the failure caused by raw values, the transformation, and its effect. Name the affected algorithm, show the formula if requested, then explain the result.

Prerequisites, vocabulary and formulas

  • Missing value: unknown entry; impute, remove, or use a supported model strategy.
  • One-hot encoding: turn a category into indicator columns.
  • Min–max: x′ = (x − min)/(max − min).
  • z-score: z = (x − μ)/σ, giving mean 0 and standard deviation 1.
  • Data leakage: using information unavailable at prediction time.

Step-by-step method

  1. Inspect types, units, missingness and target balance.
  2. Split first (or fit transformations only on training folds).
  3. Encode categories and handle missing values using training data.
  4. Scale numeric features when the method uses distances or gradients.
  5. Apply the fitted transformation unchanged to validation/test data.

Worked practice 3 — foundational calculation

Question: Features are age (20–80) and income (€20,000–€200,000). Why scale before kNN?

Model answer: Euclidean distance is dominated by the larger numerical range, income, even if age is useful. Standardising both features makes a one-standard-deviation change comparable. Fit μ and σ on training cases only, then use them for all later cases.

Question interpretation and independent practice

Prompt 1

Encode colours red, blue, green. Check: three binary columns (or two with a stated reference); do not assign red=1, blue=2, green=3 unless ordinal order exists.

Exam bridge

Outline a safe preprocessing pipeline for a labelled dataset with missing numeric values, a city category, and train/test evaluation. Check: split before fitting; impute and one-hot encode; scale where appropriate; fit all choices on training only; mention leakage.

High-value traps and corrections

Paper basis for the integrated practice: syllabus/concept practice, not claimed as an adaptation of a verified local-paper prompt.

Integrated syllabus-based practice - leakage-safe preparation [8 marks]

Scenario. A hospital model predicts readmission from age, income, ward and a “days until follow-up” field recorded after discharge. Age is missing for 8% of records and income ranges from 0 to 200,000. Specify a safe preparation pipeline.

Question-demand diagnosis: identify the temporal leak, then explain missing-value and scale treatment within a train/test split.

Fastest route: remove post-outcome information; split first; fit imputation and scaling on training only.

Worked answer: Exclude days-until-follow-up because it is unavailable when the prediction is made. Split by patient/time before learning transformations. Fit a median age imputer and, if informative, a missingness indicator on training data; encode ward categorically and standardise income using training mean and variance. Apply the fixed transforms to validation/test records. This prevents the held-out distribution, and especially future outcome-linked data, leaking into model selection.

Topic-specific trap: fitting a scaler on all rows before splitting is leakage even without an explicit label column.

  • Scaling before splitting and leaking test statistics.
  • Treating nominal category codes as numeric distances.
  • Deleting rows automatically without considering bias or lost data.

Final answer checklist

  • Did I name the data problem and the remedy?
  • Did I say transformations are fitted on training data?
  • Did I connect scaling to the algorithm?

Normalisation and distance-related preparation appear in local 2021/22 and 2023/24 papers; use 2019/20 for wider context. Exact wording is not guaranteed.
